summary.intent: Understand the memory loop architecture deeply, then design and begin implementing an MCP server that lets Claude pull memories on demand (as an alternative to hook-based push injection).
summary.outcome: Architecture questions answered thoroughly; design spec written for a two-tool MCP server (search_memories, save_memory); implementation plan created; mcp-go dependency staged; subagent dispatched to scaffold the MCP server package.

repo: Memory loop has two independent axes: mode (off/manual/auto) controls injection, activation_policy (review/auto) controls whether generated memories auto-activate.

manual mode currently has no compelling use case — auto+review policy already provides the same safety gate. The MCP server gives manual mode a real identity: no hook push, but Claude can pull via MCP.
Injection happens in UserPromptSubmit hook (lifecycle.go:282) and is gated strictly on mode == auto; there is no mid-conversation injection mechanism.
SelectRelevant uses token overlap + outcome bonus (+5 reinforced, -5 ineffective) + scope bonus (+3 personal) + cooldown penalty, packed into a 1200-byte budget with max 2 memories.

Facets are the intermediate representation between raw transcripts and memory candidates — structured signals (repeated instructions, missing context, friction points, skill opportunities, repo/workflow learnings) extracted per session before pattern analysis.
Memory records carry full provenance: source session IDs, evidence quotes, timestamps, injection counts. State lives in .entire/memory-loop.json and insights cache in .entire/insights.db.
No existing MCP server in the project — Claude Code interacts with entire purely through hooks (push model). The MCP addition flips this to a pull model.
The project uses github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go as the MCP library.
Hook installation reads/merges/writes .claude/settings.json — the MCP server registration will follow the same pattern, adding an mcpServers.entire entry.

code.finding: maybeInjectMemoryLoop exits immediately if mode != auto — manual and off modes get no injection, no staged/on-demand path exists
AddManualRecord (or ManualRecordInput) exists for creating candidate records from outside the refresh pipeline — used by the planned save_memory MCP tool

workflow: Session used superpowers:brainstorming skill before design, superpowers:writing-plans before planning, and superpowers:subagent-driven-development for execution — a structured ideate→spec→plan→execute flow.

Self-review of spec caught a real ambiguity: SelectRelevant only returns StatusActive records (passesInjectionGate), but search_memories needs to support status:candidate filter — required a separate non-scored listing code path.
Subagent-driven development chosen over inline execution for this implementation; tasks decomposed into 8 discrete units with dependency ordering.
mcp-go dependency doesn't appear in go.mod until first import — adding it via go get before writing code is premature; it will be pulled when the first import is compiled.

friction: User interrupted the assistant twice mid-response ('continue' needed twice) during the design presentation — likely due to response being cut off or tool call interruption.
AskUserQuestion tool was called multiple times during design to confirm choices, adding latency to what could have been a single consolidated prompt.
context7 MCP library docs were fetched to get mcp-go API but the transcript doesn't confirm whether the API details were accurate — implementer subagent may hit API shape mismatches.
go get for mcp-go didn't modify go.mod/go.sum because no code imports it yet — the dependency addition step was effectively a no-op until actual code is written.
open_items: Task 2: Implement mcpserver/server.go scaffold with NewServer(), checkModeGate(), placeholder handlers and mode-gating tests.
Task 3: Implement search_memories handler reusing SelectRelevant scoring plus separate listing path for candidate-status queries.
Task 4: Implement save_memory handler using AddManualRecord with fingerprint dedup; export FingerprintForRecord if not already exported.
Task 5: Create mcp_server_cmd.go cobra command and register in root.go.
Task 6: Modify hooks.go InstallHooks/UninstallHooks/AreHooksInstalled to manage mcpServers.entire entry in .claude/settings.json.
Task 7: Run fmt, lint, test:ci across the full codebase.
Task 8: Integration smoke test — build CLI, verify MCP server responds over stdio, verify hook installation writes mcpServers block.
Decide whether to remove manual mode or keep it with the new MCP-pull semantic (design says keep it, but no final confirmation from user).
TUI keybinding for staging/injecting a memory was mentioned as a future nice-to-have but not scoped into this plan.
